finding: ⭐ THE MAPPING IS DETERMINED BY THE GRAPH, NOT CHOSEN BY THIS CYCLE, and that was verified rather than taken from the item: all three ids are absent from the 77 routes in routes.json, and each target is the `primary` route for the publication those rows name — RT-ASO (primary, PUB-ASO) NOT RT-ASO-ASK (contributing, the wet-lab ask); RT-PARTNER-STRAT (primary, PUB-FUSION-PARTNER); RT-DEGRADER (primary, PUB-DEGRADER). ★ THE HARM WAS REAL AND MEASURED: four rows could never be scored at all, because apply_route_inheritance gives an unscored row the floor OF ITS ROUTE and a route the graph lacks has no floor. After the remap they inherit 71.71, 70.86, 70.86 and 35.71 — AUT-PD-006, AUT-PD-040 and AUT-PD-141 are ASO v2 manuscript and gate work, AUT-PD-005 is degrader-paper work. They were invisible to the queue, not deprioritised by it. ⛔ AND THE FIX COULD NOT BE LANDED ALONE: shrinking the population to 69 puts the pinned ceiling of 73 four above the real count, and test_the_ratchet_is_not_vacuous allows at most 2 of slack. The ceiling had to move DOWN in the same commit. That coupling is the good kind — it means a repair that shrinks the population is forced to re-pin, so the constant can only ever tighten by neglect, never loosen.

anti_gaming.how_it_applies: ⭐ A BAR WAS CHANGED AND THE DIRECTION IS WHAT MAKES IT LEGAL: MAX_UNSCORED_OPEN moved DOWN, 73 -> 69, which makes the guard STRICTER and makes this cycle's own future filings harder, not easier. route_advanced_why: ⭐ HONEST, AND NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS. This cycle wrote no science and moved no manuscript. What it did is make three ASO-v2 manuscript-and-gate rows (AUT-PD-006, AUT-PD-040, AUT-PD-141) RANKABLE for the first time — they had no score and no ranking term could reach them, so no cycle could ever be offered them. Work that the queue cannot see is work that does not happen, and the paper those rows serve is PUB-ASO, the only one with a public DOI. ⛔ It did NOT advance the ASO manuscript itself, and this field is not claiming it did.
